previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure due to recurrent tracheal and bronchial stenosis from Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. He presented with sudden shortness of breath and cyanosis at home, requiring EMS transport. He was stabilized with oxygen and nebulizers, then underwent bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and bilateral mainstem bronchi, which improved his airway patency and oxygenation. His leukocytosis resolved without antibiotics, and pain was managed with oxycodone. He was restarted on home medications, including tobramycin nebulizers and Esbriet, with a new nebulizer provided. He was discharged home with follow-up planned in one month for repeat bronchoscopy and continued management of chronic conditions.

The patient was placed on a non-rebreather over trach with 
improvements in his O2 sats up to 90%. He was given nebulizer 
treatments and respiratory remained at bedside. Pulmonary was 
consulted and determined that the patient needs a bronchoscopy 
and dilation. Of note, the patient was scheduled for dilation on 
the ___. The patient was taken to the OR and underwent an 
uneventful bronchoscopy. During the bronchoscopy, the IP team 
again encountered was known benign central airway obstruction 
with excessive granulation tissue and friable mucosa, including

controlled with iced saline and epinephrine. The patient was 
observed in the PACU where he received Decadron and Zosyn. He 
was subsequently transferred to the Internal Medicine service 
for further post operative monitoring.  
 Upon arrival to the floor, patient is doing well. He still 
complains of pain around the trachea area and chest pain with 
breathing. He is breathing comfortably on 40% FiO2. He denies
